Is the next step to stop the process, and if we do, what is the import of it? That is my worry. I am concerned. As others have spoken to, the students moving from Accra to Elubo or Wa Secondary School, when they have not been there before in his or her life — An instruction just came yesterday, and a few things would have to be bought for the children. How do we get these things sorted out? It is getting too late. 131 30th November, 2023 132 Statements Mr Speaker, however, is the remedy for Parliament to issue a counter instruction? That is my worry, and that is why I am saying that as much as I associate with this, we should also be circumspect in order not to create further confusion. Mr Speaker, if we could tidy up that statement, I have nothing against it, but it should not be said of Parliament that we are contradicting what the Ministry is saying, and that wards and parents should not respond. That is my worry. Mr Speaker: Hon Members, I do not have the final words here. I said this was just a guide, and they would refine it, and I would get it across to the Leadership before it is issued. However, it would be issued this night. They are actually listening to what is happening, and they have taken notes of your contributions, and I believe that we would incorporate all that you have expressed. With this and your kind permission, I would like to adjourn the House. Mr Agbodza: Mr Speaker, I know that it was said earlier that the Hon Minister for Food and Agriculture was not around to lead us to eulogise our gallant farmers, but that does not mean that at least, with your authority, we cannot just take the opportunity to wish our gallant farmers a 39th National Farmers’ Day. I think the Hon Majority Leader would agree with me that we could at least take some two minutes to wish our farmers a gallant 39th Farmers’ Day, thank them for feeding all of us, and wish them well. Mr Speaker, that was all I had wanted to say; that despite the fact that the Hon Minister was not here, Parliament — Mr Speaker: Very well. Hon Member, thank you so much for the timely intervention. I think it eluded us. We should at least make a Statement to commend and congratulate our gallant farmers for what they have been doing over the years. Who would like to make the Statement? The comments can come now. Mr Kyei-Mensah-Bonsu — rose — Mr Speaker: Yes, Hon Majority Leader? Mr Kyei-Mensah-Bonsu: Mr Speaker, I think what the Hon Minority Chief Whip — Mr Buah — rose — Mr Kyei-Mensah-Bonsu: Mr Speaker, am I out of order? Ei! Ei Mr Armah-Kofi Buah. [Laughter] Mr Speaker, I think what the Hon Minority Chief Whip

have been referred to by some Hon Members in their submissions. It is not this Government. Nobody has said this Government is what is causing the decadence of education. No! They have traced it even to the time of the Provisional National Defence Council (PNDC), so do not be like you are on the defence. 77 6th December, 2023 78 Statements That is why I said that I am not sure you heard sufficiently to be able to respond. Can I give you an opportunity to come back with a Statement later on education because I am very much interested in this matter? Dr Adutwum: Mr Speaker, the Statement said that there is a decline in the quality, and Ghanaians are watching us. My Hon Colleague asked a question on the change in curriculum. The curriculum has been changed. So many different things are happening now. There has been a change in curriculum, and it is the implementation of that curriculum that is leading to the improvements that we are seeing in a number of schools across the country. Mr Speaker, the literacy rate of this country, which was at a point in time two per cent for primary two students in terms of proficiency, has risen to 38 per cent. We are not where we need to be — Mr Speaker: Proficiency in what? Dr Adutwum: Reading in primary two. Mr Speaker: Reading what? Dr Adutwum: Reading. Literacy. Mr Speaker: English or Twi? Dr Adutwum: English. Mr Speaker: Is that our language? It is one of the challenges they have pointed out. We do not develop any society using another society’s language. It is something we have to look at. Please, maybe, you will need to take the Official Report, go through it and come up with a comprehensive Statement, because we are the leaders. The political leaders are here. We are those who work on the manifestoes of the various political parties. If we see that there is a problem with our educational system, we have to lead and make sure that it changes. We will all agree in this country that corruption is systemic, and so the best way of solving corruption is to change the system. We are not prepared to change that system, but we keep on blaming each other. We are talking about education, and we know the problem. Nation building is a joint effort. We have formal and informal education. Most of the contributions are based on the formal. What about the informal sector? At our family and societal levels, what do we do to assist in education? Please, it is not about now or yesterday. Generally, we have seen that we have backslid. Even with the introduction of these new policies you are talking about, we are still backsliding. The type of education we are doing is, to tell you the least, not relevant to our environment as a country. Please, I think I would give you another opportunity to come with a Statement on this matter, so that we look at it again.

issues we were concerned about here in Parliament, and the reasons we came out with a decision for the Hon Minister to be here were important. I even read that for first year students whose parents would have challenges, it would be all right for them not to go today, but they could appear on Tuesday or Wednesday because they understand that there would be challenges. 15 4th December, 2023 16 Votes and Proceedings and the Offical Report That really fortified what you just pointed out that clearly, the results that came out and the postings to the different locations — I had parents come to me over the weekend when I was in the Constituency. Their children have been posted far away and frankly, they were not ready. They were trying to make arrangements to ensure that their children are posted closer to the Western Region. So, clearly, there are challenges that these parents need time to address, and the Hon Minister for Education’s own release admitted that. Mr Speaker, so, when we make a decision here in Parliament and we all agree to bring the Hon Minister for Education, we must be united in that decision. So, what you have said is the decision of Parliament and I believe that we have to support that decision because the rules are very clear. Thank you, Mr Speaker. Mr Boamah — rose — Mr Speaker: Yes, Hon Member for Okaikwei Central? Mr Patrick Yaw Boamah: Mr Speaker, thank you. 10.48 a.m. Mr Speaker, as much as I agree with Hon Colleagues to get the Hon Minister on the Floor to respond to the concerns of Hon Members, I think without hearing the Hon Minister and the Rt Hon Speaker making a decision or giving us an idea of what he intends doing bothers me. This is because you rightly said the Hon Minister responded to your call, and I think there were some missed calls — Mr Speaker: Hon Member, I never said that the Hon Minister responded to my call. Mr Boamah: The Rt Hon Speaker said that there was an attempt to reach the Hon Minister, and I believe that we should give the Hon Minister an opportunity — Mr Speaker: Hon Member, I never said there was an attempt to reach the Hon Minister. Mr Boamah: Mr Speaker, that notwithstanding, the Hon Minister for Education must be given the opportunity to appear before the House for Hon Members of Parliament to take a firm decision on this matter. I do not want us to pre-empt matters. Yes, he has been invited and given a time to appear. We do not have to suggest that he would not appear, and that when he does not appear — Mr Speaker: Hon Member, I am sure you were not listening to the Hon Majority Leader. The Hon Majority Leader conveyed to the House that the Hon Minister will appear before the House — according to him, between 12.30 and 1.00 p.m. The time given to the Hon Minister is 12.30 p.m.; he

or a particular year of a particular Government. We are looking at the bigger picture; hence we cannot deal with this matter on the Floor of the House. So, probably, I was thinking that Mr Speaker, in your wisdom, would do some referral, that the Committee on Education should engage the Hon Minister. There, they can do a detailed assessment of the subject matter. But now that Mr Speaker has given the directive that the Hon Minister should come with a Statement, I think we should all go by that. We would urge the Hon Minister to do it. Nobody is saying that his Ministry is under judgement. We are looking at an absolute concern related to the educational sector and we are not relating it to any Government or— Mr Speaker, I think we will go by your directive, and allow the Hon Minister to come to the Floor of this House and present a Statement to this effect. 83 6th December, 2023 84 Statements Mr Speaker: Hon Members, I will allow the Hon Minister to come with a Statement on this matter and put his perspectives before the House for us to look at. Based on that, if there is the need for us to refer the matter to the subject matter Committee to sit with other stakeholders for us to review the whole educational sector, then we will do so. I think that is the proper thing to do. This is because, as you know, Statements should not be reduced to debates, they are just comments to be made. So, we would like that to be done. Hon Minister, as you come, it will be very good if you have some data that could assist the House because you are in charge of the sector. You may not make general statements like the ordinary Hon Members, so come with some data on how things are being turned around and we would all look at whether to go with the steps that are being taken now or introduce new initiatives to change things. More importantly, if you could come up with a Statement to show how the issue of values, ethics, integrity and honesty—those issues that have been raised—are being addressed, it will be important to all of us. Also, you may look at how relevant the education is now to the situation in our country. How is it helping us to solve the challenges that we face as a nation? With this, Hon Members, we have come to the end of Statements. We have other things that we have to move on to and I am to receive some important guests, so I will take a few things and hand over to the Hon First Deputy Speaker. Hon Members will recall that a few days ago, I stopped the Hon Member for Bawku Central, Mr Mahama Ayariga, from laying a Petition. I think the time is now for him to do so. Then, we will move to some other Papers to be laid, which my attention has now been

curriculum and they obeyed? He was a Deputy Minister, and he actually had to sit with his Minister and agree. Mr Speaker, so, if he does this and then comes here to tell a Cabinet Minister that he should listen to Parliament, then he is telling him that the instructions of the person who appointed him do not matter. But I think that we are not being fair to ourselves. I agree with you 100 per cent that we are the representatives of the people, that times are not normal, and that we could have extended the time a little bit, but the way and manner the instructions went out confused the general public. People were asking the same questions. Is it the case that they should listen to Parliament and let their wards wait or that the directive of Parliament supersedes that of the Hon Minister or that the Hon Minister would not have any power at all to tell us when to send our kids to school? Mr Speaker, if the Hon Minister had listened to this House and asked the children to stay home and the President called the Hon Minister to ask him what reason he allowed the kids to stay home and, therefore, shut down the schools which were to be opened on 4th December, 2023, what report would the Hon Minister give him? This is somebody who reports to the Executive and not the Legislature, even though we have an oversight responsibility over him. I want us to tread cautiously. Yes, we have every right to come out as a people and advise the Hon Minister. Let us come to this situation where, say, the Ministry of Defence would decide on a particular day to do some exercises, then Parliament comes out to say that by the powers vested in us by the people who brought us here, we are asking the Ministry of Defence to stop. I have not been in this House for too long, but at least, I have not seen anything like that before. Mr Speaker, the best I have seen here is for the Rt Hon Speaker to be petitioned, then a Committee is set up, we sit on it, and we pronounce on the Report. But, as a people, as far as I am concerned, or with what I know, we do not give counter-instructions to Executive instructions. I think that what happened this particular time, if you ask me, Mr Speaker, is too harsh on the Hon Minister. Now, there is confusion out there. Headteachers do not know whether they are reopening or not; students do not know whether they would go to school because Parliament said something which they could not decipher or the explanation did not come out well. Mr Speaker, if we continue like this, we would run a country that would have no direction at all, and I think this is what 139 4th December, 2023 140 Statements I would like to bring to the attention of the House.
